q: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to _____.
e: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to deforming forces. Several real forces can add to give the net centripetal requirement. compressing forces or shearing forces is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The study of fluids has two parts, statics and _____.
e: The study of fluids has two parts, statics and dynamics. kinematics or mechanics is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at _____.
e: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at rest. Fluid statics is about fluids at rest. motion or equilibrium is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in _____.
e: Fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in motion. Fluid dynamics studies fluids in motion; statics studies fluids at rest. rest or vacuum is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The study of the flow of liquid is called _____.
e: The study of the flow of liquid is called hydrodynamics. hydrostatics or aerodynamics is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Hydrostatics is the study of liquid at _____.
e: Hydrostatics is the study of liquid at rest. Fluid statics is about fluids at rest. flow or motion is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The volume of a liquid does not depend on pressure if the temperature is constant, hence the liquid is _____.
e: The volume of a liquid does not depend on pressure if the temperature is constant, hence the liquid is incompressible. viscous or elastic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called _____.
e: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called streamline. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. trajectory or vector line is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers with no mixing, such a flow is called _____ flow.
e: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers with no mixing, such a flow is called laminar flow. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. turbulent or viscous is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In steady laminar flow, streamlines _____ each other.
e: In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross each other. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. intersect or merge into is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In turbulent flow, the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both _____.
e: In turbulent flow, the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and direction. On a circle the velocity direction keeps turning even if the speed is steady. pressure and volume or temperature and density is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid to be _____.
e: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid to be incompressible. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. viscous or compressible is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Internal friction in fluids is called _____.
e: Internal friction in fluids is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). capillarity or surface tension is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow assumes the flow has no friction, meaning _____ viscosity.
e: Ideal laminar fluid flow assumes the flow has no friction, meaning zero viscosity. A limit as Δt → 0 is the instantaneous rate, so that increment goes to zero. maximum or constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An example of laminar flow is _____.
e: An example of laminar flow is sea breeze. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. storm or whirling water is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An example of turbulent flow is _____.
e: An example of turbulent flow is storm. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing. smooth pipe flow or sea breeze is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
Motor car brake oil is non-compressible. highly compressible or a gas is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
Gases are compressible. incompressible or non-viscous is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
